output.brief: Don't send the breach notice. The rise isn't mainly a Tessaly handling problem. Since 1 September, Corvane tags printed at Harlow Bay (on the new Fennick stock) fail automatic reading about 12% of the time. Before, it was 1.5%. Tags from other stations and Pelion's tags are unchanged at about 1.3–1.5%. Pelion shares Tessaly's crew pool and its rate is flat. Bags sent to manual encode went from about 70 to about 470 a day. Those bags now miss the lateral close, and 91% arrive after it. Auto-read bags are unchanged at about 3.8 per 1,000. The same counters printing on Brackwater stock from stores on 14–16 Oct read at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick failed at 12%. So the stock is the trigger. What we can't yet tell is whether the Fennick stock is defective or just needs different printer heat settings. Next steps: revert counters and kiosks to Brackwater stock now (about five weeks are in stores and the contract runs to 31 Dec). Then test Fennick against Teyra's settings guidance before filing any claim against Fennick. Drop the breach notice and fee withholding. Confidence is high on the mechanism and moderate on the root cause within the stock/printer-setting pair.
